page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-4 is an arm64 virtual machine offering 4 dedicated vCPUs paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware profile features no onboard GPU accelerators and includes no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Network connectivity does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio prioritizes memory capacity over processing density. Because the instance uses dedicated arm64 processor cores without hyperthreading flags or x86 instruction sets, compute execution remains isolated from shared-thread contention. The absence of local solid-state drives means storage performance depends entirely on remote block storage configurations and attached persistent disk tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-per-core density makes this instance economical for workloads that exhaust RAM long before consuming significant CPU cycles. The c4a-highmem-4 is well suited for memory-intensive applications, including in-memory key-value stores, relational database management systems, intermediate data caching, and containerized backend microservices built for Arm environments.
